headline: NRS: CHAPTER 392 - PUPILS
blurb: Nevada added its school immunization law in 1971, and it now requires a certificate showing a child is immunized against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, polio, rubella, and measles to enroll in public school, with exemptions for religious belief and medical conditions.

headline: Health District Advises of New School Immunization Requirements
blurb: The Southern Nevada Health District said new State Board of Health rules would require students entering seventh grade to be immunized against whooping cough, starting with the 2008-09 school year.

headline: Health District identifies 3rd and 4th measles cases
blurb: The Southern Nevada Health District said four measles cases had been confirmed in Clark County in 2015, the first confirmed cases there since 2011.

headline: Health District declares acute hepatitis A outbreak in Clark County
blurb: The Southern Nevada Health District reported 37 acute hepatitis A cases in Clark County in the first five months of 2019, compared with 17 in the same months of 2018.

headline: Public Health Update: Health District declares end to Hepatitis A Outbreak
blurb: The Southern Nevada Health District declared the Clark County hepatitis A outbreak over after 107 cases, 94 hospital stays, and one death.

headline: First Measles Case Reported in Clark County
blurb: The Southern Nevada Health District reported the first confirmed measles case in Clark County since 2018, in an infant who was not yet old enough to get the MMR vaccine.
